name: Arcanist
description:
You lift your staff as you utter the incantation you practiced this morning. You feel the hair stand up on the back of your neck as you begin to pull magic out of the air around you. As your lips shape the words, you feel reality itself resonating, gathering, sharpening. You are aware of the danger of this act, this plucking of invisible strings. You must rely on the accumulated wisdom of those who came before you - those who wrote down the secrets they uncovered - as well as the refinement you yourself have achieved in your own study. Here comes the hardest part - the third syllable of the fifth phrase is the hardest to get right, and things can go sideways if you don't form the vowel correctly. There, you're past it. Your practice has paid off. And now you feel the heat rising from the center of your staff. With a final utterance, a peal of force whips outward from you, knocking back the advancing fiends and - to your surprise - shattering the shop windows on either side of you. "Hmm," you think. "Stronger than last time. It seems adding that null clef made a difference." You'll update your notes after the battle. For now, you plant your feet and begin another incantation...

Arcanists approach magic like mathematicians. Magic does not need to be mysterious to be respected, appreciated, even loved. While other magic traditions emerged slowly and organically through great depths of time and experience, the Arcanist tradition is much more recent and is an endeavor to uncover and master the invisible forces that pervade our world and ourselves. An Arcanist's constant, probing analysis may not sit well with practitioners of more ancient arcane arts. Indeed, many Arcanist spells are the result of reverse-engineering spells from the older traditions, and the Arcanist practice of naming these "new" spells after themselves has certainly raised hackles across the world.

Arcanists are students of the Lingua Arcana - a written and spoken expression of sounds that is more like music notation than ordinary text. This language is very much a work in progress, and Arcanist spells can be volatile as a result. Books and scrolls are essential to any practicing Arcanist, as is their Arcane Focus: an enchanted object they must have in order to cast spells.

Arcanist is by far the broadest - and also one of the most complex - of the spellcasting mestieri. Divided across eight distinct schools, many of its spells are less potent and/or less predictable than equivalent spells from other traditions, but in exchange you get a wide breadth of possibilities. You will know many, many spells. Sometimes they will blow up in your face. You are learning, discovering, and eventually, if you stick with your studies, you may even invent new spells yourself.

You will choose your Arcanist archetype at the outset, which defines your approach to your arcane studies:

  • If you are a Hedge Mage, you are an independent, unaffiliated student of magic, who has come by an odd assortment of spells and has the freedom to pursue subsequent study in any direction you choose, though you must buy books and scrolls to continue your studies.

  • If you are a Wizard of the Tower, you have committed yourself to a powerful institution of learning which provides you with considerable resources (more MP to spend each day on your spellcasting) but which also restricts you to a prescribed course of study and demands unwavering transparency and loyalty.

  • If you are a Rune Knight, you belong to a most unusual order that combines the martial and the magical (a rare thing in Renaissance!), imbuing your gear of war with magic through the art of runic inscription.

Whichever path you choose, know that you are choosing to delve into regions of understanding that many others regard as forbidden or sacred. Where all this inquiry will lead is uncertain.

Play an Arcanist if you want to:

  • Approach magic as a system to be understood and extended, casting spells with knowledge rather than faith or instinct, growing more powerful the more you learn, but also never being entirely certain of exactly what your next spell will do.

  • Get your fingers into all of the magical pies, learning a wide range of magic until you have a spell for practically every situation.

  • Bring complexity and whimsy to the battlefield, teleporting through walls, stepping into pocket dimensions, and generally bending reality in unexpected ways.

Questions to consider when making an Arcanist:

  • Where did they encounter the idea that magic is a structure, not a mystery? Was it a mentor, a text, a failed spell that made no sense until they worked out why?

  • How do they describe their spells when asked? Do they give technical explanations, or do they use poetic language?

  • What is their relationship to other magical traditions? Do they regard them with respectful curiosity, or with something closer to frustration?

  • What is the first spell they hope to write themselves one day? What gaps do they see in the existing corpus of Arcanist spells?

  • What does it feel like when a spell misfires? For others, unexpected results might register as the divine will or nature's capriciousness. For an Arcanist, every failure is a calculation error. How do they process that?

novizio.description: You have set out on your chosen approach to the learning the Lingua Arcana, have obtained your first Arcane Focus and have learned a handful of spells. You have some limited experience using magic in combat, though it may only have been in controlled, practice scenarios.
novizio.abilities: Arcane Focus and choose your Arcanist archetype: Hedge Mage, Rune Knight, or Wizard of the Tower. Each archetype determines how you select your initial abilities.
novizio.spellcasting: You must be wearing or wielding your Arcane Focus and must be able to speak in order to cast spells.
novizio.gratuiti: A spellbook or scroll case, a quill and ink, robes and - if you choose - a hat.
